messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed in the observable universe is the exoplanet **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × Jupiter’s radius** (about 18,000 km).  Its mass is estimated to be a few times that of Jupiter, but it is still below the de‑uterium‑burning limit that separates planets from brown dwarfs, so it is classified as a planet rather than a substellar object.

> **Key facts about HD 100546 b**  
> • **Radius:** ~ 2.5 R_Jupiter (≈ 18,000 km)  
> • **Mass:** ~ 5–10 M_Jupiter (estimates vary)  
> • **Orbit:** ~ 10–20 AU from its host star (a few times the distance of Saturn from the Sun)  
> • **Discovery:** 2014, using high‑contrast imaging with the VLT (Very Large Telescope)  

While there are many massive exoplanets and even larger substellar objects (brown dwarfs and low‑mass stars), HD 100546 b remains the largest confirmed planet in terms of radius. If you’re interested in the most massive exoplanets or brown dwarfs, let me know!
